claim: UAB reallocates a fixed sampling budget across questions using vote entropy of the first K samples with a marginal-greedy solution to a concave coverage surrogate, improving average accuracy by +2.3% over uniform allocation and up to +5.5% on individual benchmarks.
stance_target: L3: uncertainty-routed budgets exist for math/logic via sampled consistency
scope_conditions: Five open models 1.5B-27B, five reasoning benchmarks, no code
quoted_support: UAB improves average accuracy by + 2.3 % over uniform allocation, and achieves gains of up to + 5.5 % on individual benchmarks, with the largest gains in low-resource settings.
numbers: Qwen2.5-1.5B Avg 47.0 vs Uniform and Random 43.1

breadth.confidence_families: Vote entropy of K initial samples (answer disagreement); baselines NLL, Max-token NLL, ANLL, length, random, uniform (Table 4-5)
breadth.reasoning_models: not present (searched: reasoning-model comparison; benchmarks are 'reasoning' tasks but models are standard open-weight)
breadth.elicitation_formats: Sampled-consistency (vote entropy) vs logit NLL; verbalized: 0 hits
breadth.benchmarks: MATH500, Formal Logic, DeepScaler, GSM8K, Graded Arithmetic (Table 4); no code (HumanEval/LiveCodeBench/MBPP 0 hits)
breadth.label_source: Answer match with majority vote correctness
breadth.label_independence: Oracle(q) = smallest sample count whose majority vote is correct (Table 5)
breadth.calibration_metrics: Accuracy at N=4; %Under/%Over-C/%Over-W vs oracle (Table 5); no ECE

claim: Against an oracle (smallest sample count whose majority vote is correct) at N=4 on Qwen2.5-1.5B, vote-entropy UAB (K=2) leaves 10.5% of questions under-allocated versus 13.3% for Uniform and 14.1% for an oracle-difficulty variant.
stance_target: allocation quality vs oracle and uniform
scope_conditions: Table 5, mean over five datasets, excluding questions unsolved in 16 samples

scope_conditions: Intro; full-text grep verbalized 0, HumanEval 0, LiveCodeBench 0
